files.role: Row-ID location metadata, immutable shared inline bytes with lazy digest, and file-range descriptor. Public items are reexported by format although row_ids is a private child module.
ranges: SPDX plus Deref, Arc/OnceLock, Bytes, core DeepSizeOf/Error/Result, serde traits and generated pb imports. Reexports the three canonical core lineage field-ID constants rather than redefining their values.

Public ExternalFile has path:String, offset:u64 and size:u64 with Debug/Clone/PartialEq/Eq/Serialize/Deserialize/DeepSizeOf derives. Docs assign it to fragment-reuse index details. It is a descriptor only: construction here does not validate paths/ranges/overflow or perform IO, and RowIdMeta has no External variant.

Public Clone InlineRowIds privately holds Arc<InlineRowIdsInner>; inner stores Bytes and OnceLock<[u8;32]>. Comments motivate content identity because fragment IDs can be reused and scans clone fragments. The Arc shares the Bytes handle and digest memo; actual byte backing can be a separately retained fetched-buffer slice, not necessarily bytes embedded in the same Arc allocation. Statements about count_from_mask and scan frequency are caller rationale, pending consumer inspection.

digest returns a reference to32-byte BLAKE3 hash of the exact encoded byte sequence, initialized lazily by shared OnceLock; cloned wrappers share initialization/result. bytes returns &Bytes without mutation. This identifies encoded content, not a canonical decoded sequence; equal logical rows with different encodings may hash differently, and finite hashes are not a mathematical uniqueness guarantee. Hash work scales with encoded length on first use and is reused thereafter.

From<Bytes> allocates a new Arc inner with moved Bytes and empty OnceLock, without an explicit payload copy. From<Vec<u8>> first delegates to Bytes::from then the same constructor. Separate constructions get separate memos even when bytes are equal; payload-allocation details of Bytes are external dependency behavior.

Deref exposes immutable [u8]. Debug delegates to Bytes formatting. PartialEq first accepts shared-Arc pointer identity, otherwise compares byte contents; Eq is marker implementation. Digest is neither inspected nor initialized by equality/Debug. No DerefMut or direct mutable byte access is exposed.

Serialize delegates to Bytes only; Deserialize obtains Vec<u8> from the deserializer and maps through constructor, producing a fresh empty digest memo. Memo state does not enter serialized data. The generic serde format is chosen by the caller; JSON representation is pinned by the local test.

Wrapper DeepSizeOf delegates to Arc for identity deduplication; inner delegates heap children only to Bytes. Core Arc adds size_of inner once per Context and excludes Arc counters, while Bytes charges visible length once per starting pointer, not the retained backing-buffer allocation; OnceLock inline storage is included via inner size. This is an estimate, not retained RSS. Supporting implementations: rust/lance-core/src/deepsize.rs:90-98; rust/lance-core/src/deepsize.rs:182-189.

Public RowIdMeta derives Debug/Clone/PartialEq/Eq/Serialize/Deserialize/DeepSizeOf and has Inline(InlineRowIds) or Column. Column docs specify hidden ROW_ID_FIELD_ID in a fragment data-file entry, one ID per physical row in offset order, enabling page-level reads. Actual file lookup/column validation/reader algorithms are pending Fragment/rowids analysis.

TryFrom generated RowIdSequence returns Result but both known arms succeed: InlineRowIds(data) wraps raw encoded bytes, ColumnRowIds payload is ignored and becomes Column. It does not decode sequences, validate column presence or test feature flags. An absent protobuf oneof cannot be represented by this input enum; handling None belongs to its caller.

cfg(test) imports super and Fragment. Digest fixture compares equal bytes from separate wrappers, changed final byte, byte equality and repeated digest contents. Assertions show selected examples, not collision freedom or initialization count.

Clone-sharing fixture checks identical byte and digest pointers for clones; separately constructed equal bytes have distinct byte pointers. A fresh clone initializes a memo then original returns equal digest contents. No concurrent stress or counted hash invocation is performed.

Bytes-sharing fixture slices16..48 from64-byte buffer, wraps a clone, asserts contents and same start pointer. A second8-byte slice differs in deep_size_of by24; this pins length-based accounting, not total retained backing capacity.

Serialization fixture requires exact JSON {"Inline":[7,8,9]}, roundtrips through serde, then embeds metadata into Fragment and roundtrips via protobuf conversion. Digest is absent from output. Fragment conversion implementation remains pending, and no disk file is read/written or historical fixture loaded. Tests were read, not executed.
files.limits: Facade visibility is established by rust/lance-table/src/format.rs:26-29. Build Bytes configuration is at rust/lance-table/build.rs:19-21; actual fetched-buffer decoder and content-key consumers remain pending. The active Column metadata is separate from the legacy-frozen behavior boundary; no source was changed.

files.role: Public format-layer protobuf Transaction wrapper and conservative operation classification for schema-validation decisions; distinct from the transaction module builder type.
ranges: SPDX and module documentation motivate avoiding dependence on higher lance layers and postponing protobuf conversion. The comment says crate-local, but the actual pub struct and public format facade expose this type outside the crate; internal-use README policy is a separate issue. Imports generated pb.

Clone/Debug/PartialEq Transaction contains a public inner:pb::Transaction; as_pb borrows it immutably. It is not an independent normalized Rust operation model, and direct public mutation can construct any protobuf state. No validation occurs in this wrapper.

may_change_schema delegates to operation_may_change_schema(&inner). Docs motivate permitting non-schema-changing operations, including deletes, to repair existing invalid primary keys, while conservatively classifying unknown operations. This method returns a policy boolean and performs no primary-key validation or commit.

Standalone classifier accepts &pb::Transaction, independent of encoded length or optional inline-manifest storage. For UpdateConfig it returns true when either field_metadata_updates or field_metadata is nonempty. A nonempty map containing an empty update still qualifies; table config-only changes do not. Comments explain a size-dependent commit bug avoidance, but actual caller ordering remains pending.

Returns false for exactly Append, Delete, CreateIndex, Rewrite, DataReplacement, ReserveFragments, Update, UpdateMemWalState, UpdateBases and DataOverlay. Wildcard returns true for every other recognized variant and None (including unknown wire operations that decode to no known arm). It examines only operation variant and UpdateConfig field-map emptiness, not payload consistency or data validity.

From<format::Transaction> for pb::Transaction moves inner out; reverse From wraps by value. Neither encodes wire bytes, clones payload, checks sizes nor validates schema despite the write-boundary serialize wording in docs.

cfg(test) imports prost::Message. Exempt-delete test clones a default Delete transaction, enlarges tag to4MiB and asserts encoded_len grows beyond100 times small; both classifications remain false. It does not invoke manifest inline threshold logic, encode bytes or actually commit.

DataOverlay exemption fixture uses default payload and asserts classifier false. The comment describes a prior invalid-primary-key upgrade scenario, but this local test does not construct that dataset or run validation.

UpdateConfig fixture with config_updates only is exempt. Inserting field_metadata_updates entry0 holding an empty UpdateMap makes it schema-changing. Legacy field_metadata branch is implemented but not separately tested here.
Overwrite default payload must classify true; default transaction with no operation also true. This is not an exhaustive operation matrix test. All tests were read, not executed.
